newsitem.title: Australia: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: TWO PEOPLE UACCOUNTED FOR AFTER VIC FIRES
Two people still remain unaccounted for after 85 bushfires left a trail of destruction across Victoria.
Two others died in the fires, and more than 45 houses were destroyed.
Rescue workers are sifting through the remains of the burnt out properties, in case any more bodies remain hidden.
The two people unaccounted for are believed to be from Fern Gully in the Dandenong Ranges east of Melbourne.
Meanwhile a new blaze has broken out on 100 hectares of land near Mansfield in the north east of the state.
Insurance experts say they're expecting more than ten-million dollars worth of claims, and the state government says families affected can apply for an immediate cash grant of 700 dollars.
ENTRENCHED OPPOSITION TO GST SAYS PM
Prime Minister John Howard says there's a misguided belief in some sectors of the community that tax reform will solve all of Australia's economic problems.
Speaking on Channel Nine's Today program, John Howard said recent calls for a goods and services tax show how easily people forget.
Mr Howard says those pushing for a GST need to realise there's still a lot of entrenched community opposition to the concept.
He reiterated his election promise not to introduce such a tax in his first term of government, but has not ruled out further tax reform after that.
HOWARD CONFIDENT OF RESOLUTION AT WIK MEETING
The Prime Minister, John Howard, has gone into a meeting between State and Territory leaders saying he has some well developed ideas on resolving uncertainty about native title.

Mr Howard says he understands how precious Native Title is to Aboriginal Australians but there can't be a situation where some farmer can't build dams on their property without the permission of native title holders.

Northern Territory Chief Minister Shane Stone and the Premiers of Western Australia and Queensland have developed a plan which would see the common law native title rights extinguished and remaining rights spelt out in legislation.
But ACT Acting Chief Minister Gary Humphreys sees no problem with the High Court decision and says the issue should be resolved through negotiation
New South Wales premier Bob Carr says the proposals by other states are options to be considered, but there must be a national solution.
WIK SUMMIT UNDERWAY IN CAIRNS
The Wik summit gets underway in Cairns today with Aboriginal leaders saying that while negotiation is the answer extinguishment of native title is out of the question.
The summit will be opened by the Wik people and will hear the native title concerns of Aboriginal, mining and pastoral groups.
ATSIC commission Geoff Clark says Aboriginal expectations are not as high as they once were in terms of ambit claims and they are keen to find common ground.
WRITERS SIGN DECLARATION AGAINST LIBRARY CHANGES
Twenty-five of Australia's leading writers have signed a declaration claiming government cuts are eroding their rights.
The writers, including Dorothy Hewett, Donald Horne and Ruth Park, are upset at a proposal for a 25 year limit on payments to authors whose works appear in public libraries.
The authors claim their livelihood is being threatened.
The cuts to the Public Lending Right Scheme are expected to save the government about half-a-million-dollars a year.
TIGHT QUARTER-FINAL AT OZ OPEN
At the Australian Tennis Open, a tight quarter finals match is underway between Mary Jo Fernandez and Belgium's Dominique Van Roost.
The scores are level at three games all, and both players have dropped serve once in the first set.
Also competing for a semi-finals berth today are Romania's Irina Spirlea and title favorite, Martina Hingis.
In the men's singles, Goran Ivanisevic meets Thomas Muster, and tonight Pete Sampras takes on the unseesed Albert Costa.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
